items.request: Explain in plain words that a language model reads a run of text as whole-number token ids and, at every position, scores each possible next token. Name the idea once as next-token prediction. Then show that the model's forward function takes a grid of integers, batch by time, and say that everything else serves this one job.
items.why: A short reading with cited lines is the best way to state the idea and map it to the signature.

items.request: Explain the model's fixed menu of tokens (vocab size 50304, which is GPT-2's 50257 padded up) and its longest accepted input (block size 1024). Explain the check that rejects inputs longer than the block size. Worked example: length 1025 fails, length 1024 passes.
items.why: This beat is a definition plus a small worked check, both of which read well as text.

items.request: Flow diagram with shapes. Token ids (b,t) go to a token embedding lookup giving (b,t,n_embd). A position embedding is added to it. The sum goes through a loop over the transformer blocks, then a final layer norm. Every box after the lookup is labelled (b,t,n_embd).
items.why: The data flow and constant shapes are a structure best seen as a diagram.

items.request: Numpy notebook. Take one vector of length 4 and a random matrix standing in for the final linear layer with a vocab of 6 tokens. Compute the logits (one score per token). Print them and note they are raw scores, not probabilities, since they can be negative and do not sum to 1. Let the learner change the vector and rerun.
items.why: Trying the numbers by hand shows that logits are raw scores, one per vocab token.

items.request: Numpy notebook with batch 1, time 5, embedding 4, vocab 6. Build x of shape (1,5,4) and a head matrix. Show the full logits shape (1,5,6), as when training with targets, where cross entropy scores each position against the true next token. Then slice only the last position, x[:, [-1], :], giving logits shape (1,1,6). Print both shapes.
items.why: Comparing the two shapes on real numbers makes the last-position shortcut concrete.
